M4GJ: Dasan das = servant of servants. Panihare = water-carriers. ||8||1||
I call myself the servant of Your servants; keep me a water-carrier for Your servants. ||8||1||
Nanak, the slave of Your slaves, says, I am the water-carrier of Your slaves. ||8||1||
Says Nanak, the slave of Yours slaves, O Lord, I am the water carrier of Your attendants.
Sri Guru ji says: we are the (panihare) water-carriers of those who are the servants of Your servants. ||8||1||
7NEB: Ram = O Ram! Paathar = hard-hearted, stone-hearted. Nirguniare = without virtue.
O my Ram! We beings are hard-hearted and empty of virtue.
O Lord, I am an unworthy stone.
O my Omnipresent Lord, I am meritless like the stone.
O Ram! We were stones without virtue.
CA6M: Milae = unite. Ham pahan = us stones. Sabad = through the Word. Tarai = carry across. ||1|| Rahau ||
Show mercy, show mercy, and unite us with the Guru. Carry us stones across (the world-ocean) through the Guru's Word. ||1|| Rahau ||
The Merciful Lord, in His Mercy, has led me to meet the Guru; through the Word of the Guru's Shabad, this stone is carried across. ||1||Pause||
The Merciful Master has mercifully made me meet the Guru and by Guru's teaching, I, the stone, am saved. Pause.
When the Guru, the treasure of mercy, in His mercy united us with Himself — we who were like stones, the Guru gave us His teaching and carried us across. ||1|| Rahau ||
EB3L: Satgur = O Guru! Drirrae = make firm in the heart. Mailagar = sandalwood. Mailagar malgare = the sandalwood of sandalwood, finer even than sandalwood.
O Guru! Make Parmatma's Name firm (in my heart); this Name is very sweet and finer even than sandalwood (in bringing coolness).
The True Guru has implanted within me the exceedingly sweet Naam, the Name of the Lord; it is like the most fragrant sandalwood.
The True Guru has enshrined within me the very sweet Name of the Lord, which is cool and fragrant like the sandal.

The True Guru makes the supremely sweet Name firm, and it is the (malgare) sandalwood even of (mailagar) sandalwood — meaning it is supremely cooling, or is sandalwood itself. And becoming the borax of reflection, it melts away the dross of attachment and aversion and purifies the gold of the heart.
BHS5: Naamai = through the Name alone. Surat vaji hai = this awareness grows strong, that. Dah dis = in the ten directions. Mushk = the fragrance of musk. Gandhare = fragrance. ||1||
Only through the blessing of the Name does this awareness grow strong: that the fragrance of Parmatma's being is spreading in every direction in the world. ||1||
Through the Name, my awareness extends in the ten directions; the fragrance of the fragrant Lord permeates the air. ||1||
Through the Name, I have obtained the knowledge of ten directions and I now realise the Fragrant Lord is perfuming all.
Through the Name alone the knowledge of Hari, the (gandhare) fragrant One, has spread through the ten directions, and His praise is spreading like musk. ||1||
PHKP: Nirgun = beyond the three qualities, untouched by the three qualities of Maya. Gur = through the Guru. Neeke = good. Samare = can be enshrined in the heart.
O Prabhu! Your praise is sweet; the three qualities of Maya cannot touch it. Through the Guru, the beautiful words (of Your praise) can be enshrined in the heart.
Your unlimited sermon is the most sweet sermon; I contemplate the most Sublime Word of the Guru.
My Master, the Guru's sublime Gurbani, is Yours discourse of detachedness and sweet discourse and I reflect thereon.
When we have kept hold of the Guru's beautiful words, then among all stories Your story beyond the qualities has felt supremely sweet.
KAN1: Gavat gavat gae = began to sing at every moment. Gur = by the Guru. Nistare = carried across. ||2||
Those who began singing Parmatma's virtues at every moment — as they sang His virtues, the Guru carried them across (the world-ocean). ||2||
Singing, singing, I sing the Glorious Praises of the Lord; singing His Glorious Praises, the Guru saves me. ||2||
Sing, sing and hymn I the Lord's praise. By hymning the Lord's praise, the Guru emancipates the mortal.
Those who have sung Hari's virtues at all three times — through singing His virtues the Guru has carried them across. ||2||
FN1Q: Bibek = discernment of good and bad (skilled in it). Sam darsi = {sam = equal, the same} seeing all alike (with love). Tis = that Guru.
The Guru is skilled in discerning good and bad deeds; the Guru looks on all beings alike, with love. One should meet that (Guru), putting away (all the) doubts (of one's mind).
The Guru is wise and clear; the Guru looks upon all alike. Meeting with Him, doubt and skepticism are removed.
The Guru is discriminating and the Guru looks upon all alike. Meeting with him, the mortal's doubt is dispelled.
The Guru who holds discernment is (guru) great and sees all alike. Meet Him, putting away doubt — meaning do not hesitate over caste or family.
NS9F: Mileeai = one should meet. Utare = putting away. Miliai = {remember the difference between 'mileeai' and 'miliai'} if one meets. Param pad = the highest spiritual state. Hau = I. Kai = to. ||3||
If one meets the Guru, the highest spiritual state is reached. I am a sacrifice to the Guru. ||3||
Meeting with the True Guru, I have obtained the supreme status. I am a sacrifice to the True Guru. ||3||
Meeting with the True Guru, I have obtained the Supreme status. To the True Guru, I am a sacrifice.
Through meeting the True Guru, the highest state has been reached; we are a sacrifice to the True Guru. ||3||
UTW7: Pakhand = (religious) shows (to gather Maya and the like). Kar = doing. Kar kar = doing again and again. Bharme = wander. Jag = in the world. Buriare = very bad.
(Beings) keep wandering, always putting on (religious) shows (to gather Maya and the like). This greed and this (religious) show are very bad (enemies) in the world.
Practicing hypocrisy and deception, people wander around in confusion. Greed and hypocrisy are evils in this world.
People wander about practising hypocrisy and deception. Evil are avarice and hypocrisy in this world.
Putting on show after show, they have wandered through the lands. Through greed and hypocrisy (jag) beings have become wicked.
5L3D: Halat = in this world. Palat = in the world beyond. Hovah = are {plural}. Sir = on the head. Maare = strikes, keeps killing spiritually. ||4||
In this world and the next (these are always) causes of suffering; (because of them) the messenger of death stands over (beings') heads and keeps killing (all) spiritually. ||4||
In this world and the next, they are miserable; the Messenger of Death hovers over their heads, and strikes them down. ||4||
In this world and the yonder one, They become miserable and standing over their head, the Death's courier smites them.
Greed, hypocrisy and the rest bring suffering in this world and the next. Yama, the bringer of death, stands over their head, striking blows. ||4||
X1CW: Ugvai = rises, dawns. Aal = {alaya} home. Aal jaal = the net of household affairs. Bikh = poison, bringing spiritual death. Bisthare = spreads.
(When) the day dawns, (the greedy being) begins the household affairs and the spread of Maya, which brings spiritual death;
At the break of day, they take care of their affairs, and the poisonous entanglements of Maya.
With the day-break, they take care of their household affairs and poisonous worldly entanglements.
When the day dawns, people take up the net-like affairs of the house and spread the deeds of Maya, which is poison.
A1AE: Rain = night. Supnantar = lost in dreams. Supnai bhi = in the dream too. Bikh saare = tends the poison. ||5||
(when) night comes, (the being, according to the affairs of the day) is lost in dreams; in dreams too they tend only the sufferings that bring spiritual death. ||5||
When night falls, they enter the land of dreams, and even in dreams, they take care of their corruptions and pains. ||5||
When the night falls, they enter the dreamland and even in dreams they look after their afflictive and mortal riches.
When night comes, this being, lost within a dream, tends even in the dream the poisons that are suffering — meaning they dream of the objects of the senses. ||5||
UJ81: Kalar khet = a field where no crop grows because of alkali, a field of the heart where the seed of the Name does not grow. Koorr = attachment to perishable things. Jamaia = sowed. Khalvare = threshing floors, heaps.

The field of the heart of those cut off from Parmatma is alkaline (where the seed of the Name cannot grow). (They) keep sowing only attachment to perishable things in it, and gather only heaps of attachment and Maya.
Taking a barren field, they plant falsehood; they shall harvest only falsehood.
Taking a barren field, man sows falsehood therein; therefore he shall gather all falsehood in his thrashing floor.

In the alkaline field — the impure heart — they (jamaia) sowed falsehood, deeds done for reward. And all became heaps of falsehood — meaning they suffered through births. Or: the spiritual practice said to be done in an impure heart is false, and the realisation claimed is false too.
5Z9A: Saakat nar = people cut off from Prabhu. Sabh = all. Bhookh bhukhane = hungry and hungry, always hungry, always tormented by craving. Jam dar = at Yama's door. Jandar = mighty. Thaadhe = standing. ||6||
(The result is that) those cut off from Prabhu stay tormented by craving at every moment, and stand at the door of mighty Yamraj (stay in the power of the messengers of death). ||6||
The materialistic people shall all remain hungry; the brutal Messenger of Death stands waiting at their door. ||6||
All the apostate persons remain extremely hungry and the tyrant Death's courier stands ever at their door.
All those who have gone astray are hungry with the hunger of craving; at their door stand the messengers of Yama, rods in hand. ||6||
4T2B: Manmukh = people who follow their own mind. Bikh karaj = a debt that brings spiritual death. Veechare = reflecting.
On the heads of those who follow their own mind a debt (of vices) that brings spiritual death stays mounted; only by enshrining the Guru's Word in the mind is this debt paid off.
The self-willed manmukh has accumulated a tremendous load of debt in sin; only by contemplating the Word of the Shabad, can this debt be paid off.
The perverse person has incurred an immense debt of sins. Reflecting over the Name, this debt is liquidated.

On the heads of the self-willed, greedy for the objects of the senses, is mounted a very heavy debt of three kinds — to the ancestors and the others. The debt is paid off only if one reflects on the Guru's teaching.
8ZT4: Karaj ke mangeeye = debt-collectors, those whose debt one is caught under, the messengers of death. Kar sevak = making servants. Pag lag = falling at the feet. Vaare = were held back. ||7||

(When a person takes the Guru's shelter, then) all these messengers of death, the collectors of the debt, are made servants (of those who take the support of the Guru's Word), set at their feet and held back. ||7||
As much debt and as many creditors as there are, the Lord makes them into servants, who fall at his feet. ||7||
As many are the demandants of debt; so many the Lord makes his slaves, who repair to his feet.
All the gods, rishis and ancestors who came demanding the debt — Parmeshvar has made them servants of the devotees, to fall at their feet. ||7||
DLN1: Jagannath = Master of the world. Sabh jantar = all beings. Upae = created. Nak kheeni = nose-pierced. Nathhare = with a nose-string, under control.
(O brother, what power do beings have?) All these beings are created by Prabhu, the Master of the world; all of them are in His power, (like cattle) with pierced noses.
All the beings which the Lord of the Universe created - He puts the rings through their noses, and leads them all along.
All the beings that the Lord of the world has created; tearing open their noses and loading them all with snaffles, the Lord makes them bow before Him.
Parmeshvar has created all beings, and (nak kheeni) piercing their noses He has made them all (nathhare) bound by the nose-string — meaning He has brought them under His command.
GL7N: Nanak = O Nanak! Khinchai = pulls. Bhavai = pleases. ||8||2||
O Nanak! As Prabhu pulls (the beings' nose-string), as is the will of beloved Ram, so (beings) must walk. ||8||2||
O Nanak, as God drives us on, so do we follow; it is all the Will of the Beloved Lord. ||8||2||
Nanak, as the beloved Lord Master wills and as He drives, so are we driven, so are we driven.
Sri Guru ji says: according to their deeds, as it pleases beloved Prabhu Ram, so He pulls, and one has to walk accordingly. ||8||2||
9LQ5: Ram = O Ram! Har = O Hari! Amritsar = in the pool of the water of the Name that gives spiritual life. Naavare = bathes.
O Ram! O Hari! (The person who, by Your grace,) bathes (their mind) in the pool of the water of Your Name, which gives spiritual life —
The Lord has bathed me in the pool of Ambrosial Nectar.
O my Lord-God, bathe You me in the tank of the Nectar-Name.
O brother, Hari has bathed us in the pool of nectar, which is the true company.
EVJ0: Satgur = in the Guru. Giaan = understanding of spiritual life. Majan = bath. Neeko = beautiful, good. Mil = meeting (the Guru). Kalmal = sins. Utare = washes off. ||1|| Rahau ||
(that person), meeting (the Guru), washes off (all their) sins and vices. The understanding of spiritual life (through the Guru) is itself the beautiful bath in the Guru (-pool). ||1|| Rahau ||
The spiritual wisdom of the True Guru is the most excellent cleansing bath; bathing in it, all the filthy sins are washed away. ||1||Pause||
The True Guru's Divine knowledge is the excellent ablution. Obtaining it, the filth of sins is washed off. 'Pause.
The knowledge gained through the True Guru is the beautiful bath. Meeting the True Guru, all the sins, heavy and small, have been washed off. ||1|| Rahau ||
KN5N: Gun = effect, influence, benefit. Adhikaee = great. Parr = reading. Sooa = {shuka} parrot. Udhare = carries across.
The influence of company is very great; (see:) the parrot, reading ('Ram Naam' from Ganika), carried Ganika across (the ocean of vices).
The virtues of the Sangat, the Holy Congregation, are so very great. Even the prostitute was saved, by teaching the parrot to speak the Lord's Name.
The advantage of the holy company is very great. The whore was emancipated by teaching the parrot to utter the Lord's Name.
The virtue of company is very great indeed. Through teaching the (sooe) parrot, Hari carried Ganika across; or, the company of the fine parrot a great soul gave her carried Ganika across.
ULEP: Parsan paras = {sparsha = touch} a most excellent touch (of Sri Krishna ji's feet). Kau = to. Baikunth = in Baikunth. Sidharai = reach. ||1||
Kubija received the excellent touch (of Sri Krishna ji's feet); (that touch) took her all the way to Baikunth. ||1||
Krishna was pleased, and so he touched the hunch-back Kubija, and she was transported to the heavens. ||1||
Being pleased, Krishan trampled on the hunch-back and this touch took her to the True Realm.
The untouchable Kubija, whom Krishna ji touched — He took her with Him and departed to Baikunth. ||1||
CTT7: Putr prat = for the son. Keeni = done. Keh = saying again and again. Bolare = calls.
Ajamal's love for his son (Narayan is famous in the world. Ajamal) called (his son) by the name Narayan (saying "Narayan", his love grew for Narayan Prabhu too).
Ajaamal loved his son Naaraayan, and called out his name.
Ajamal bore love to his son and shouted forth as Narain. N.B. The word Narain means God and Narain was the Name of his son, too.
Ajamal loved his son, and called him by the name Narayan.
6YH5: Kai man = in the mind of. Bhai = pleased, was liked. Bhavni = faith. Kankar = {kinkara} servant. Jam kankar = the servants of Yamraj, messengers of death. Maar = striking. Bidare = destroyed. ||2||
(Ajamal's) love pleased the mind of the beloved Master, Prabhu Narayan; He struck the messengers of death and drove them off (from Ajamal). ||2||
His loving devotion pleased my Lord and Master, who struck down and drove off the Messengers of Death. ||2||
His faith pleased my Lord's mind and He smote and expelled the myrmidons of death.
That feeling pleased my Thakur's mind, and He struck down the messengers of death and drove them away. ||2||
GYL1: Kathai = says (only) by mouth. Kath = saying by mouth.
But if a person only talks, and talking only preaches to others (they gain nothing themselves); what they say they do not enshrine in their own mind.
The mortal speaks and by speaking, makes the people listen; but he does not reflect upon what he himself says.
Man utters and uttering makes people hear, but he reflects not over that what he utters.
This person speaks, but speaking, only tells it to others. The teaching they themselves speak, they do not keep — meaning they do not take it on themselves.
CMZ4: Dirrta = firmness, conviction. Naam = through the Name. Nistare = (the Guru) carries across. ||3||
When a person sits in the holy company (of the Guru), faith takes root in them; (the Guru, joining them) to Parmatma's Name, carries (them) across (the world-ocean). ||3||
But when he joins the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation, he is confirmed in his faith, and he is saved by the Name of the Lord. ||3||
When the mortal meets with the society of saints, then obtains the staunchness of faith and the Lord's Name ferries him across.
If they meet the true company, then (dirrta) conviction comes to them that the Name of Hari Ram alone carries across. ||3||
EBVP: Jab lag = as long as. Jeeo = life. Pind = body. Sabat = whole, intact. Tab lag = till then {'lagu' and 'lagi' mean the same}. Na samare = does not tend, does not care for the spiritual life.
As long as (the union of) life and body stays intact, till then (the person cut off from Prabhu) does not enshrine (Prabhu's remembrance) in the heart;
As long as his soul and body are healthy and strong, he does not remember the Lord at all.
As long as his mind and body are whole and full, so long, he remembers not his God, in the, least.
As long as the body is whole, till then this being does not keep hold of the Lord's Name even a little.
EUYM: Mandar = in the house. Aag = fire. Koop = well. Panihare = the one who draws water. ||4||
(take their state to be like that of a person) who, when fire breaks out in their home and palace, then digs a well and draws water (to put out the fire). ||4||
But when his home and mansion catch fire, then, he wants to dig the well to draw water. ||4||
But, when the house and mansion catch fire, is that the time for the water-man to dig a well to draw water from that.

(Jab) When the fire of time comes and touches (ghar mandar) the body, then this being (kadh koop) digs a well and (kadhai panihare) draws water — that is, tries to put out that fire with the water of realising Parmeshvar — but it is not put out. So to put out that fire, the well of worshipping Parmeshvar is needed beforehand. ||4||
BQB2: Saakat siu = with a person cut off from Prabhu. Man = O mind! Mel = connection, company, sitting and standing together. Jin = which (saakat). Bisare = has forgotten.
O my mind! The person who has wholly forgotten Parmatma's Name (is a saakat) — never make company with (that) saakat,
O mind, do not join with the faithless cynic, who has forgotten the Name of the Lord, Har, Har.
O man, associate you not with the mammon-worshipper, who has forgotten the Lord God's Name.
Do not join your mind with the saakat. ☬ Question: who is a saakat? ☬ Answer: one who has forgotten the Names of Har Har.
GQFX: Dasai = is stung. Taj = leaving. Parare = further away. ||5||
because a person is stung by the saakat's words as by the sting of a snake or scorpion. One should leave (the company of) the saakat and stay far, far away from them. ||5||
The word of the faithless cynic stings like a scorpion; leave the faithless cynic far, far behind. ||5||
The word of the mammon-worshipper stings like a scorpion. Leave you the apostate far away.
The words of saakats sting like a scorpion; so leave saakats far, far behind. ||5||

8H6X: Lag = falling (at the Guru's feet). Lag lag = falling again and again. Preet lagai = brought forth love (in the heart). Sadhu sang = in the Guru's company. Savare = made their lives good.
(Those who,) falling (at the Guru's feet) again and again, brought forth great love (for Prabhu's feet in their hearts), and, living in the Guru's company, made their lives good,
Fall in love, fall deeply in love with the Lord; clinging to the Saadh Sangat, the Company of the Holy, you will be exalted and embellished.
Embrace, embrace you love and embrace you great love for your Lord. Clinging to the saints, you shall be embellished, O man.

(Lag lag) Mixing again and again, they grew great love for saakats, but found no peace. When, (lag) joining the company of the holy, they grew love, then the saints set all their affairs right — meaning they brought dharma, wealth, desire and liberation to completion.
RY9C: Sat kar = knowing to be true. Mane = accepted. ||6||
(who) built full faith in the Guru's words — those people are very dear to Parmatma. ||6||
Those who accept the Word of the Guru as True, totally True, are very dear to my Lord and Master. ||6||
They, who accept the wards of the Guru as absolutely true, are very dear to my Lord.
Those who have accepted the Guru's words as true, with firm faith, have become very dear to my Thakur. ||6||
2Z8G: Poorab janam = in a previous birth. Parchoon = little by little (good deeds). Naam = in the Name. Piare = loves.
The person who in a previous birth earned good deeds little by little (through their blessing now too) has formed a love for Prabhu's Name,
Because of actions committed in past lives, one comes to love the Name of the Lord, Har, Har, Har.
By virtue of bits of good deeds done in the previous births one loves the Name of God, the Lord Master, in this life.
Those who in earlier births earned (parchoon) meritorious deeds — to them the Names Har Har have felt dear.
DLKF: Gur prasad = by the Guru's grace. Amrit = giving spiritual life. ||7||

and by the Guru's grace they have found the nectar of the Name, which gives spiritual life. That person (always) praises the nectar of the Name and enshrines only the nectar of the Name in the heart. ||7||
By Guru's Grace, you shall obtain the ambrosial essence; sing of this essence, and reflect upon this essence. ||7||
By the Guru's grace, man obtains the immortalising Name-Nectar. This Nectar's praise, he hymn and this Nectar he reflects upon.
Those who by the Guru's grace have found the nectar of the Name sing it with love and reflect on it with love. ||7||
M0W2: Har = O Hari! Sabh = all. Lalan = O beloved! Laal gulare = O beautiful beloved!
O Nanak! O Hari! O beloved! O beautiful beloved! (All beings and creatures) are all Your forms alone, Your colours alone.
O Lord, Har, Har, all forms and colors are Yours; O my Beloved, my deep crimson ruby.
O my deep red, jewel-like beloved Lord-God, all the forms and colours, are Yours.
All forms of Hari and colours of Hari are made by You alone. O my (lalan) beloved, crimson and rosy — that is, supremely blissful!
1CCD: Deh = You give. So = that colour. Kia = what power? ||8||3||
Whatever colour You give (to a being), that colour takes hold (of them). These poor beings have no power of their own. ||8||3||
Only that color which You impart, Lord, exists; O Nanak, what can the poor wretched being do? ||8||3||
As is the colour, You givest, O Lord! That alone becomes manifest, What can the poor man do O Nanak?
As You give love, so this person receives it. Sri Guru ji says: what are these poor beings, that they could do anything? ||8||3||
59KP: Ram = O Ram! Prabhu = O Prabhu! Rakhvare = You become the protector.
O my Ram! O my Prabhu! (Whomever You show grace,) You bring to the Guru's shelter and become their protector (from vices),
In the Sanctuary of the Guru, the Lord God saves and protects us,
Seeking the Guru's protection, the Lord-Master so saves the mortal,
O brother! Those who have come to the Guru's shelter — Prabhu has become their protector.
LLY0: Kunchar = elephant (a gandharva turned into an elephant by a curse). Taduai = by the crocodile. Pakar = seizing. Oopar = high {adjective}. Kadh = pulling out. Nistare = saved. ||1|| Rahau ||
just as, when the crocodile seized the elephant and dragged it away, You lifted it up, pulled it out and saved it (from the crocodile's grip). ||1|| Rahau ||
as He protected the elephant, when the crocodile seized it and pulled it into the water; He lifted him up and pulled him out. ||1||Pause||
as he had saved the elephant who prayed to Him stretching forth his trunk out of the water, on being seized and thrown in the water by the crocodile. Pause.

Just as the crocodile seized the elephant and dragged it into the water — when it raised its (kar) hand, its trunk, above the water and cried the word "Ram", then both — that is, the elephant and the crocodile — were especially carried across. ||1|| Rahau ||
SGVE: Ati neeke = very beautiful. Man = in the mind. Kar = bringing forth. Dhare = gives support.
Prabhu's devotees are of very beautiful life; Prabhu brings forth faith (in their mind) and gives them the support (of His Name).
God's servants are sublime and exalted; they enshrine faith for Him in their minds.
Very greatly sublime are the Lord's slaves. Your install their Lord's in their mind with faith.
Prabhu's servants are very, very beautiful, because they hold Hari in their minds with faith.
2902: Prabh = by Prabhu. Man = in the mind. Bhavai = pleases. Paij = honour. ||1||
Prabhu Himself has brought forth faith and devotion (in His servant); the servant feels dear to His mind; Prabhu Himself saves His servant's honour. ||1||
Faith and devotion are pleasing to my God's Mind; He saves the honor of His humble servants. ||1||
Faith and devotional service are pleasing to my Master's mind and he saves the honour of His serfs.
Faith and devotion please my Prabhu's mind; so He sets right His servants' (paij) honour, or pledge — meaning He fulfils it. ||1||
LFQR: The servant of Prabhu who is engaged in Prabhu's service and devotion sees Prabhu's expanse alone everywhere;
The servant of the Lord, Har, Har, is committed to His service; He sees God pervading the entire expanse of the universe.
The Lord Master's slave yokes himself to His service and perceives the Lord contained in the whole world.
Those who are servants of Parmeshar in mind and speech stay engaged in service; they see Brahm alone in all the (pasare) world.
B2B7: Purakh = the all-pervading Prabhu. Nihare = sees. ||2||
to them that one all-pervading One is seen everywhere (they see that) Prabhu Himself is looking on all beings with a gaze of grace. ||2||
He sees the One and only Primal Lord God, who blesses all with His Glance of Grace. ||2||
He beholds the only one Lord, who looks upon all alike.
The one to whom the One Being, Parmatma, is seen as (ik) without a second, sees all with that single gaze. ||2||
357P: Ravia = pervading. Thaai = in places. Sabh jagat = the whole world. Cheri = (like) a handmaiden. Samare = tends.
The Master Hari Prabhu fills all places; He tends the whole world like a handmaiden.
God, our Lord and Master, is permeating and pervading all places; He takes care of the whole world as His slave.
God, the Lord Master is pervading all the places and takes care of the whole world as His handmaid.
Knowing that the able Thakur Hari pervades all places, they (samare) regard the whole world as His handmaiden and Parmeshar as the Husband.
VQ1B: Daan devai = gives gifts. Keere kare = made worms. ||3||
Prabhu, the source of mercy, Himself shows mercy to all beings and gives gifts to all; in the stones too He Himself creates worms (and brings them their food). ||3||
The Merciful Lord Himself mercifully gives His gifts, even to worms in stones. ||3||
Of Himself the compassionate Lord mercifully gives gifts, even to the worms and insects in the stones.
He who is the home of mercy gives gifts in His mercy. The worms He has made inside the stone — even to them He brings food. ||3||
WK9G: Vaas = fragrance. Muskaee = of musk. Bhram = in delusion. Bhoola = gone astray. Mirag = deer. Sinnghare = keeps butting with its horns, keeps sniffing about.
(Within the deer itself) there is the great fragrance of musk, but, led astray by delusion, the deer goes searching (for that fragrance in the bushes). (This is the state of the soul-bride too.
Within the deer is the heavy fragrance of musk, but he is confused and deluded, and he shakes his horns looking for it.
Within him is the great fragrance of the musk, but deluded by doubt, the deer horns the bushes.

With the illustration of the deer he shows that Parmeshar is within. The deer has the great scent of musk in its navel, yet, led astray by delusion, it (sinnghare) sniffs the bushes. Just so, the witnessing consciousness is in the heart.
21T5: Ban ban = every forest. Phir = wandering. Gur poorai = by the perfect Guru. Ghar = in the home. ||4||

Prabhu dwells right within her, but the poor one) grows weary searching and searching, wandering from forest to forest. (In the end) the perfect Guru (showed her Prabhu dwelling) in her own home (and) carried her across (the world-ocean). ||4||
Wandering, rambling and roaming through the forests and woods, I exhausted myself, and then in my own home, the Perfect Guru saved me. ||4||
Wandering through and seeking, searching woods and forests, l was tired, but the Perfect Guru emancipated me in my very home.

The deluded understanding grew weary searching again and again in forests and waters, but Parmeshar was not found. When the perfect Guru was met, He showed Him within the (ghar) heart itself and carried them across. ||4||
44WN: Amrit = the water of the Name that gives spiritual life. Saare = keeps, finds.
(The Guru's) Bani is (the Sikh's) Guru; the Guru is present in the Bani. In (the Guru's) Bani is the life-giving water of the Name (which the Sikh keeps in their heart at every moment).
The Word, the Bani is Guru, and Guru is the Bani. Within the Bani, the Ambrosial Nectar is contained.
Gurbani is the embodiment of the Guru and the Guru is the embodiment of Gurbani. In the whole of Gurbani is contained the Nectar.
The Guru is the form of the Bani, and the Bani is the form of the Guru, because the nectar is in the Bani (saare) everywhere.
98XR: Gur kahai = the Guru speaks. Maanai = accepts, builds faith. Partakh = openly, surely. ||5||
The Guru speaks the Bani; (the Guru's) servant places faith in that Bani. The Guru surely carries that Sikh across the world-ocean. ||5||
If His humble servant believes, and acts according to the Words of the Guru's Bani, then the Guru, in person, emancipates him. ||5||
If the attendant acts up to what Gurbani enjoys, the Guru in person(truly) saves him.
When the Guru speaks the Bani and the servant accepts it, then the Guru carries them across, plainly. ||5||
4CWV: Sabh = everywhere. Pasria = pervading. Man = in the mind. Khavare = eats.
Parmatma fills and is present everywhere (but the being does not grasp this; the being) eats the fruit of the deeds sown in their mind (and suffers),
All is God, and God is the whole expanse; man eats what he has planted.
The Lord is among all and pervading all over is the Lord. He makes man eat what he has sown.
The whole world is Brahm, and Brahm is spread out within the world — meaning all that pervades is Brahm. He makes this mind eat what it has sown — meaning He makes it undergo the fruit of its deeds.
2BPD: Dukhia = pained. Chandrahans = a king's son whom Dhristbudhi tried to have killed, but who by mistake had his own son killed. Looki = with a firebrand, with fire. Jare = burns. ||6||
just as Dhristbudhi, wishing harm again and again on the good Chandrahans, burnt down his own house with a firebrand. ||6||
When Dhrishtabudhi tormented the humble devotee Chandrahaans, he only set his own house on fire. ||6||

As for example, Dhirstbudhi saint annoyed saint Chanderhaus. However, in an attempt to destroy Chanderhaus, he set his own house on fire. (Note: As per Hindu mythology, Chanderhaus was the son of king Dharma. Dhristbudhi bore ill-will for Chanderhaus and

As the devotee Chandrahans was troubled by the minister Dhristbudhi — for that very offence Dhristbudhi burnt down his own house with the (looki) fire of envy. Chandrahans was the son of a king named Sudharam. By fate, Dhristbudhi grew envious and wished to have him killed. Madan Singh was Dhristbudhi's son; he was killed in Chandrahans' place, and Chandrahans gained the kingdom. This story is told at length in the Bhagatmal, or the Mahabharat. ||6||
NQ8U: Kau = to. Antar rid = in the heart. Lochai = longs. Saas = breaths {plural}. Nihare = watches over.
Prabhu's devotee keeps longing to see Prabhu in their heart; Prabhu (too) keeps protecting (His) servant-devotee at every moment.
God's humble servant longs for Him within his heart; God watches over each breath of His humble servant.
The Lord's slave longs for Him in his mind and the Lord watches every breath of his.
The servants long for Prabhu within the heart. And Prabhu watches over His servants breath by breath — meaning whatever word they speak, He fulfils at that very moment.
GKF4: Drirrae = settles firmly. Jan peechhai = those who follow the servant. Nistare = carries across. ||7||
At every moment, in His grace, Prabhu keeps firming the feeling of devotion in His devotee's heart; He carries across the world too, which walks in His devotee's footsteps. ||7||
Mercifully, mercifully, He implants devotion within his humble servant; for his sake, God saves the whole world. ||7||
In His mercy, mercy, the Lord establishes His devotion within him and for His slave's sake, He saves the world.
Vahiguru, the treasure of mercy, in mercy makes devotion firm in His servants. Following behind those servants, He carries many (jag) beings across. ||7||
YWZ0: Thakur = Master. Aape = Himself. Srist = world, creation.
The Master Prabhu Himself shows Himself in the form of the world; He Himself makes beautiful the creation He has made.
God, our Lord and Master, is Himself by Himself; God Himself embellishes the universe.
The Lord Master is all by Himself and the Lord Himself embellishes the world.
In all three times the able Master is Himself alone. Prabhu Himself has made the creation — meaning He made it in freedom.
WF5C: O servant Nanak! Prabhu Himself is present everywhere; in His grace He Himself carries (beings across the world-ocean). ||8||4||
O servant Nanak, He Himself is all-pervading; in His Mercy, He Himself emancipates all. ||8||4||
Of Himself, the Lord is pervading everywhere, O slave Nanak and showing His mercy, He Himself emancipates the mortals.
Sri Guru ji says: He Himself, and He alone, moves in all as the power of consciousness. On whom He casts His gracious gaze, He Himself carries them across. ||8||4||
VPN4: Ram = O my Ram! Lehu ubare = save me.
O my Ram! Show mercy and save (me from the attacks of vices) (save me in the same way),
Grant Your Grace, Lord, and save me,
Showering Yours benediction, O Lord, save You me,
O Ram! In Your mercy, keep us safe from the world.
AJHX: Pakar = seizing. Aani = brought. Laaj = shame. Laaj nivare = saved from the shame of being stripped. ||1|| Rahau ||
as (when) the wicked seized Draupadi and brought her, O Hari, You saved her from the shame of being stripped. ||1|| Rahau ||
as You saved Dropadi from shame when she was seized and brought before the court by the evil villians. ||1||Pause||
as You, O Lord-God, had saved Daropadi from shame, when she was seized and brought in the court by the miscreants.
Just as the wicked seized Draupadi and brought her into the court — O Hari, remover of all hardship! You took away the shame Dushasan would have brought on Draupadi. ||1|| Rahau ||
0QW5: Jachak = beggars. Maagau = I ask. Piare = O beloved!
O beloved Hari! Show mercy; we are beggars (at Your door); I ask one gift (from Your door).
Bless me with Your Grace - I am just a humble beggar of Yours; I beg for a single blessing, O my Beloved.
I am a beggar and a servant of Yours door, O my Beloved and ask for a boon from You. Show You, The mercy, to me.
O beloved Parmeshar! We, Your beggars, ask one gift of You; show us mercy.
671H: Nit = always. Sardha = longing. Satgur ki sardha = longing to meet the Guru. Mo kau = me. Har = O Hari! Gur mel = unite with the Guru. Savare = set (my life) right. ||1||
(In my mind) there is always a longing to meet the Guru; O Hari! Unite me with the Guru (and) set (my life) right. ||1||
I long constantly for the True Guru. Lead me to meet the Guru, O Lord, that I may be exalted and embellished. ||1||
I ever long for my True Guru. Lead me You to the Guru-God, that I may be embellished.
My mind always has faith in the True Guru. So, O Hari! Unite me with the Guru, who would set me right. ||1||
J7XE: Saakat karam = the deeds of a person cut off from Parmatma. Matheeai = is churned. Jhol jhulare = churns again and again.
The deeds of a person cut off from Parmatma are (as useless) as churning water. The saakat (as it were) keeps churning only water.
The actions of the faithless cynic are like the churning of water; he churns, constantly churning only water.
The deeds of an infidel are like the churning of water and he daily agitates water.

The deeds of saakats are like churning water: no ghee comes out, only froth. So they do not reach the essence of the self; they get the froth of sensual pleasure, churning water every day and watching the froth swirl.
LXRR: Mil = joining. Param pad = the highest spiritual state. Kadh = drawing out (from milk). Gatkare = gulps, eats with relish. ||2||
But the person who, joining the holy company, has reached the highest spiritual state (as it were) draws butter (from milk) and relishes the butter. ||2||
Joining the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation, the supreme status is obtained; the butter is produced, and eaten with delight. ||2||
Meeting the society of the saints, one is blessed with the supreme status and taking out butter, he eats it with relish.
The Gurmukhs who, joining the true company, have reached the highest state have drawn out the (makhan) bliss of the self and are (gatkare) enjoying it. ||2||
HXAG: Nit = always. Kaia = body. Majan = bath. Mal = rubbing. Deh = body. Savare = sets right, makes clean.
The person who kept bathing the body always, who keeps rubbing and rubbing the body alone to make it clean,
He may constantly and continually wash his body; he may constantly rub, clean and polish his body.
Ever, ever man washes his body and ever the rubs, cleanses and polishes the body.
The self-willed have bathed the (kaia) body every day and rub and rub the body to make it fine — meaning they are wrapped up in the body.

D409: Man = in the mind. Bhae = felt dear. Chaar = beautiful. Phokat = empty, useless. ||3||
but the Guru's words do not feel dear in their mind — all these beautiful (bodily) adornments of theirs stay empty. ||3||
But if the Word of my True Guru is not pleasing to his mind, then all his preparations and beautiful decorations are useless. ||3||
If the word of my True Guru is not pleasing to his mind, then all his beauteous decorations are, in vain.
My True Guru's words did not please their mind. Their beautiful adornments — that is, all their practices — are (phokat) empty. ||3||
FHEW: Matak = with a swaying step, joyfully, in spiritual steadiness. Chal = walk, walk the journey of life. Sakhi = O companion! Saare = keep, enshrine in the heart.
O companion! O friend! Keep the Master Prabhu's virtues enshrined in your heart, (and so) walk the journey of life in spiritual steadiness.
Walk playfully and carefree, O my friends and companions; cherish the Glorious Virtues of my Lord and Master.
Walk you with and dalliance, O my mates and comrades and contemplate you over the virtues of my Lord.
O beloved Gurmukh companion! Walk Prabhu's path slowly, slowly, with love, and keep hold of my Thakur's virtues.
ZGXH: Gurmukh = taking the Guru's shelter. Seva = devotion. Prabh bhai = is pleasing to Prabhu. Mai = to me (too). Satgur = O Guru! Lakhare = show, give the understanding. Alakh = the Prabhu whose true form cannot be told. ||4||
O companion! Service and devotion done in the Guru's shelter are dear to Prabhu. O True Guru! Give me (too) the understanding of the unseen Prabhu. ||4||
To serve, as Gurmukh, is pleasing to my God. Through the True Guru, the unknown is known. ||4||
The service of the Supreme Guru, pleases my Lord, Through the True Guru, I have known the Unknowable Lord.
The service of the Gurmukhs has pleased my Prabhu; so the True Guru has shown me (alakh) Parmatma. ||4||
DHYG: Nari = woman. Purakh = man. Sabh = in all. Sabh = everywhere. Purakh murare = the all-pervading Hari {mur-ari}.
O companion! (Whether it is) a woman (or) a man, (whether) a man (or) a woman, in all, everywhere, the one all-pervading Parmatma alone is dwelling;
Women and men, all the men and women, all came from the One Primal Lord God.
Women and men and all the men and women have welled up from the one Lord, the Enemy of pride.
(Nari) nature and (purakh) Ishvar — that is, from Purakh and Prakriti — man and woman have all arisen. On true reflection, all are the one Murari, the Being; there is no difference at all.
T4T2: Ren = the dust of the feet. Man = in the mind. Bhai = felt dear. Mil = meeting. Mil har jan = meeting the saints, only by meeting the saints. Nistare = carries across. ||5||

but the person to whom the dust of the saints' (feet) feels dear in (their) mind — only them does Prabhu carry across the world-ocean. O companion! Only through meeting the saints does Prabhu carry one across. ||5||
My mind loves the dust of the feet of the humble; the Lord emancipates those who meet with the Lord's humble servants. ||5||
My mind loves the dust of the feet of the saintly persons. The Lord God emancipates the mortals, who associates with His slaves.
Those whose minds love the dust of the saints — meeting those people, whoever chants Hari's Name, O Hari, You have carried them across. ||5||
9PL9: Gram = village. Nagar = city. Sabh = in all places. Rid antar = within the heart itself. Bhare = searched, found.

O companion! I have wandered and looked in village after village, city after city, in all places (Parmatma is not found by searching outside like this); the saints have found Parmatma in their own heart.
From village to village, throughout all the cities I wandered; and then, inspired by the Lord's humble servants, I found Him deep within the nucleus of my heart.
I wandered from village to village and through all the cities, but through the Lord's slaves I found God in my very mind.
I wandered through every (gram) small settlement and (nagar) large settlement, all the (gram) gatherings, and Hari was not found; through the saints He has been found within the heart itself.
ZA2M: Upai = bringing forth. Mo kau = me. Milae = join. Gur = through the Guru. Nistare = carry across. ||6||
O Hari! Bringing forth faith (in me too), join me too (through the Guru) to Your feet; carry me too across the world-ocean through the Guru. ||6||
Faith and longing have welled up within me, and I have been blended with the Lord; the Guru, the Guru, has saved me. ||6||
Faith and confidence have welled up within me and the Great Guru-God has emancipated and blended me with the Lord.
The One worthy of faith has brought forth faith in the heart and united the seekers. The Guru, the form of Hari, (gur) great and worthy of worship, will carry me across too. ||6||
CBTU: Pavan = breath. Pavan soot = the thread of breaths, the string of breaths, all one's breaths. Neeka = beautiful, good. Satgur = in the Guru (joining). Veechare = reflecting, holding in awareness.

O companion! The person who, (joined) to (the feet of) the Guru and holding the Guru's Word in their awareness, has made the string of their breaths beautiful (through the blessing of remembering the Name) —
The thread of my breath has been made totally sublime and pure; I contemplate the Shabad, the Word of the True Guru.
The entire lineage of my breaths the True Guru has rendered sublime and I now reflect over the Name.
Reflecting on the True Guru's Word, they have made the whole thread of the life-breath excellent — that is, fruitful.
GQRB: Nij ghar = in one's own home, within the self. Jai = going, settling. Amrit ras = the water of the Name that gives spiritual life. Bin naina = without eyes, without the eyes of Maya, putting away attachment to Maya. Nihare = seeing. ||7||
putting away attachment to Maya and seeing the world (as it really is), and settling within, they have drunk the nectar of the Name, which gives spiritual life. ||7||
I came back to the home of my own inner self; drinking in the ambrosial essence, I see the world, without my eyes. ||7||
Arriving at my own home, I now drink in the immortalising Name-Nectar and see the world within, without eyes.
(Jai) reaching their own true self, they have drunk the nectar that is the bliss of the self. Without these eyes, with the eyes of understanding, they have seen the world as the form of Brahm. ||7||
V4L7: Tau = Your. Ees = O Isha! O Ishvar! Saakau = I can. Ham = we worldly beings. Nik = tiny. Keere = worms.
O Prabhu! I cannot describe Your virtues. You are a beautiful temple; we beings are tiny worms living within it.
I cannot describe Your Glorious Virtues, Lord; You are the temple, and I am just a tiny worm.
Yours excellences, O Lord, I can describe not. You are the Temple and I a tiny worm.
O Ishvar! I cannot describe Your virtues. You are the form of a temple and we are small worms — meaning we live on Your support.
W6CT: Gur melhu = bring about union (with) the Guru. Mai man = my mind. Dheere = may settle. ||8||5||
O Nanak! If mercy comes upon me and I am united with the Guru, my mind, chanting and chanting the Name, will stay settled (at Your feet) forever. ||8||5||
Bless Nanak with Your Mercy, and unite him with the Guru; meditating on my Lord, my mind is comforted and consoled. ||8||5||
Show You mercy to Nanak and make me meet the Guru contemplating my Lord, my soul is comforted.

Sri Guru ji says: O Vahiguru! In mercy, unite me with the Guru. Through Him, O Ram, may I chant You, because only by chanting You does the mind (dheere) settle — that is, without chanting the mind stays restless. ||8||5||
FGQA: Mere man = O my mind! Bhaj = remember. Thakur = Master Prabhu. Agam = unreachable. Apar = limitless.
O my mind! Keep remembering the virtues of the unreachable and limitless Master Prabhu,
O my mind, vibrate, meditate on the inaccessible and infinite Lord and Master.
O my soul, meditate you on the Inaccessible and Infinite and virtueless.
O my mind! Worship the Name of the unreachable, limitless Thakur.
D7CL: Ham = we beings. Nirguniare = empty of virtues. Gur = through the Guru. Nistare = carry across. ||1|| Rahau ||
(and keep saying: O Prabhu!) We beings are sinners, very empty of virtues. In Your grace, carry us across (the world-ocean) through the Guru (bringing us to the Guru's shelter). ||1|| Rahau ||
I am such a great sinner; I am so unworthy. And yet the Guru, in His Mercy, has saved me. ||1||Pause||
I am a great sinner and virtueless. The Guru has mercifully emancipated me. Pause.
We were sinners and very much without virtue; in His grace the Guru has carried us across. ||1|| Rahau ||
3V8S: Sadhu purakh = a good person, a saint. Sadh jan pae = (the one who) gains the company of the saints. Binau = {vinaya} request. Karau = I make. Gur = O Guru!
O beloved Guru! The person who gains the company of the saints becomes a Gurmukh too; I too make a request (at Your door: grant me too the company of the saints, and)
I have found the Holy Person, the Holy and humble servant of the Lord; I offer a prayer to Him, my Beloved Guru.
I have met with my sweet, Guru the saintly person and the holy man and make a supplication before him.
The (sadhu purakh) True Guru, whom the exalted have found — before those beloved of the Guru I make one request.
7MZG: Pooji = capital, stock, wealth. Nivare = may remove. ||1||
give me the wealth of Parmatma's Name as capital, which would remove all the craving for Maya and all the hunger for Maya from within me. ||1||
Please, bless me with the wealth, the capital of the Lord's Name, and take away all my hunger and thirst. ||1||
Bless you me with the capital and wealth of the Lord's Name, Wherewith thirst and hunger are all effaced.
Give me the wealth of Ram's Name as (pooji) capital. That capital will take away all craving for the things of this world and all hunger for the next. ||1||
92FS: Pachai = burns. Patang = moth. Mrig = deer. Bhring = bumblebee. Kunchar = elephant. Meen = fish. Indri = (meaning) vice, desire. Pakar = seizing. Saghare = destroyed, killed.
The moth burns (on the lamp's flame); the deer, the bumblebee, the elephant, the fish — these too are each brought under the power of one vice or desire and killed.
The moth, the deer, the bumble bee, the elephant and the fish are ruined, each by the one passion that controls them.
Moth, deer, bumble-bee, elephant and first are dominated and ruined by one passion each.
The moth, the deer, the bumblebee, the elephant, the fish — each one sense has seized and destroyed all these.
8W6Q: Panch bhoot = the five demons, lust and the rest. Sabal = sa-bal, strong, mighty. Hai = are. Dehi = in the body. ||2||
But in the human body all five of these demons, lust and the rest, are strong (how can a person stand against them?). Only the Guru, only the True Guru, takes away these vices. ||2||
The five powerful demons are in the body; the Guru, the True Guru turns out these sins. ||2||
But in the body are the five powerful demons. The Great True Guru turns out these evil doers.
In the body there are five at once, great sinful demons, lust and the rest, with all their strength. Those who are in the True Guru's shelter have had them (nivare) removed. ||2||
2N0E: Sodh = examining, testing, reflecting. Pukare = declare loudly.
The Vedas and Shastras have been examined and looked at many times, (and) the words that Narad and other rishis and sages declared with force (about the way of life) —
I searched and searched through the Shaastras and the Vedas; Naarad the silent sage proclaimed these words as well.
The six Shastras and the four Vedas I have carefully searched and seen, and Narad, the silent sage, too utters the same words.
I have searched and searched the six Shastras and four Vedas and seen; they too say only this, and the sage Narad and others cry out this same word.
2Z5U: Gat = high spiritual state. Gur = by the Guru (alone). Nistare = to carry across. ||3||

(those too have been examined; but the real point is this, O brother:) only when you learn to remember Parmatma's Name will you reach the high spiritual state; the Guru has carried (countless beings across the world-ocean) only in the holy company. ||3||
Chanting the Lord's Name, salvation is attained; the Guru saves those in the Sat Sangat, the True Congregation. ||3||
That in the society of the saints and through the Guru's grace, man is emancipated and delivered, by uttering the Lord's Name.

That word is this: O brother! Only by reading Ram's Name will you reach liberation. But keep the holy company, then you will reach the Guru; He will carry you across by giving the teaching of Ram's Name. ||3||
RBSH: The person in whose heart love for the Beloved Prabhu has formed (longs for union with Him like this): as the lotus looks to the sun (and blossoms, as)
In love with the Beloved Lord God, one looks at Him as the lotus looks at the sun.
He, who enshrines affection for his Beloved Lord, beholds Him as the lotus does the sun.
Those who have love for the Beloved Prabhu keep looking to Him as the lotus looks to the sun.
WRKQ: Mer = mountain. Naachai = dances. Unvai = bends low (to rain). Ghan = much. Ghanhare = clouds. ||4||
when the cloud bends low (to rain), then (seeing the clouds come over) the high mountains, the peacock dances wildly. ||4||
The peacock dances on the mountain, when the clouds hang low and heavy. ||4||
When the descending clouds roar, the pea-cock greatly dances on the summer mountain.

When the Guru, the cloud, (unvai ghan) bends low and (ghanhare) thunders — that is, in mercy gives the teaching — then the peacock, the most fit seeker, standing on the (mer) high mountain Sumer of love, dances — that is, with all attention on Brahm, discerns Brahm. ||4||
KSU8: Saakat = a person cut off from Parmatma. Bis = poison. Biskare = poisonous.
The person cut off from Parmatma (is, as it were, a poisonous tree); however much nectar you pour on it, its branches and flowers will all stay poisonous.
The faithless cyinc may be totally drenched with ambrosial nectar, but even so, all his branches and flowers are filled with venom.
Though the mammon-worshipper be greatly irrigated with ambrosia, even then all its branches and flowers become venomous.

Even if much nectar is poured on the saakat — that is, even if they are given the finest teaching — the branches, the senses, and the (phool) deeds, are (biskare) black with sensual craving; meaning all the deeds of saakats come with sin.
UMAF: Nivah = bow, deal humbly. Seti = with. Chherr = provoking. Kadhai = brings out {singular}. Bikh = poison. Khare = bitter. ||5||
The more people deal humbly with the saakat, the more they provoke and bring out bitter poison (from within). ||5||
The more one bows down in humility before the faithless cyinc, the more he provokes, and stabs, and spits out his poison. ||5||
The more man bows in humility before a perverse person, the more he provokes, pricks and spits out poison.
The more a good person bows before the saakat, the more they provoke and provoke — that is, pick quarrels — and speak (khare) bitter, painful words like poison. ||5||
XBGS: Mil = joining. Mil raheeai = one should stay joined. Bolah = speak {plural}. Par upkare = words for others' good.
(So, instead of making company with the saakat,) one should stay joined with the saints, with the Gurmukhs. The saints speak only good words for the good of others.
Remain with the Holy man, the Saint of the Saints, who chants the Lord's Praises for the benefit of all.
Remain you united with the holy Guru, the saint of the saints, who utters the Lord's praise for the public good.
Stay joined with the (sadh) finest, the (sant) peaceful ones. They speak only virtues, for the good of others.
ETYW: Santai = to a saint. Milai = meets {singular}. Bigsai = blossoms. Jal mil = meeting the water. ||6||
As lotuses blossom on meeting water, so when a saint meets another saint, their mind blossoms. ||6||
Meeting the Saint of Saints, the mind blossoms forth, like the lotus, exalted by obtaining the water. ||6||
Meeting with the Guru, the holiest of the holy, my soul blossoms like the Lotus, which is embellished by obtaining the water.
When a saint meets a saint, the mind is glad, as lotuses meeting water (savare) blossom at dawn. ||6||
2FMA: Lobh lahar = the wave of greed. Sabh = pure, sheer. Suan = dog. Halak suan = a rabid dog. Sabhah = all.
The wave of greed is sheer rabid dog; (as) a rabid dog keeps ruining everyone (by biting them), (so a greedy person keeps making others greedy in their company too).
The waves of greed are like mad dogs with rabies. Their madness ruins everything.
The current of avarice is all like the dog's madness. This madness has spoiled everything.
The wave of greed is like the madness of a (suan) dog. That rabid dog ruins all its companions — meaning a greedy person makes their companions greedy too.
EKVC: Kai deeban = in the court of. Khabar = {this word always ends in 'i'}. Hoee = {the letter 'h' carries two vowel signs, (o) and (u); the actual word is 'hoee', to be read here as 'huee'}. Gur = through the Guru. Kharrag = sword. Giaan = understanding of spiritual life. ||7||

(When the person, to be saved from this greed, takes the Guru's shelter and cries out at Prabhu's door, then) news (of their plea) reaches Parmatma's presence; through the Guru, Parmatma takes the sword of the understanding of spiritual life and kills the rabid dog of greed within them. ||7||
When the news reached the Court of my Lord and Master, the Guru took up the sword of spiritual wisdom, and killed them. ||7||
When the news reached the court of my Lord. then taking up the sword of Divine knowledge, the Great-God did slay it.

When word reached my Vahiguru's (deeban) court, the holy company, it took up the (kharrag) sword of knowledge, Sri Sahib, and killed the greedy dog. Meaning, when a greedy person comes into the holy company too, they reflect and leave them. ||7||
XVWG: Prabh = O Prabhu! Mai = me. Rakh = save. Rakhahu = save. Dhare = showing.
O my Prabhu! Save me too (from this dog of greed); save me, save me; in Your grace, save me too.
Save me, save me, save me, O my God; shower me with Your Mercy, and save me!
Save, save, save You me, O my Master and rescue me by showering Yours benediction.
With mind, speech and body this alone is the prayer: O Prabhu! Show me grace and save me.
7J1X: Dhar = support. Kaee = {feminine; masculine 'koee'}. Mai satgur = my (support is) the Guru alone. Chhaka = a group of six. ||8||6|| Chhaka 1 ||
O Nanak! (Say:) I have no other support. The Guru alone is my support; the Guru alone carries across (keep me in the Guru's shelter). ||8||6|| Chhaka 1 ||
O Nanak, I have no other support; the Guru, the True Guru, has saved me. ||8||6|| First Set of Six Hymns||
Nanak, I have not any other support. The Great True Guru has ferried me across.
Sri Guru ji says: I have no other shelter. The revered True Guru alone will carry me across. ||8||6|| Chhaka 1 ||
